newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian bonds close easier after 30-yr auction.
newsitem.headline: Canadian bonds close easier after 30-yr auction.

text.p: Canadian bonds ended softer on Wednesday as investors absorbed the supply of C$1.3 billion 30-year bond auction after Tuesday's rally.

New York-based I.D.E.A. analyst Harvinder Kalirai said the Bank of Canada's auction had an average reception as investors were less inclined to buy when the market was near all-time highs. But bonds could roll higher after today's pause, he added. "I think the general tone of the market is fairly good. We had a huge run," Kalirai said.
Canada's 30-year benchmark bond slipped C$0.30 to C$120.20 to yield 6.463 percent.
The U.S. 30-year bond fell 8/32 to yield 6.43 percent and the spread between the two narrowed to three basis points from four at Tuesday's close.

The Government of Canada said the 8.0 percent bond auction posted an average yield of 6.467 percent at a price of C$120.141. The government had rolled over C$1.3 billion of its benchmark 30-year bond.

Investors took a breather after Tuesday's rally on bullish economic commentary by U.S. Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan. Greenspan, who finished his Congressional remarks today, had little to add, analysts said.
"Dealers were relieved that Greenspan's testimony didn't scare anybody," Kalirai said.
MMS International analyst Rob Palombi added that the market would be seeking direction now that fears of a short-term interest rate hike in the U.S. and Canada had receded.

In other prices, Canada's 10-year benchmark bond lost C$0.33 to reach C$109.79 to yield 5.921 percent. The U.S. 10-year bond fell 6/32 to yield 6.15 percent, so the negative spread between the bonds widened to 23 basis points from Monday's close.
